subject.title: fix(reply): strip leaked current-message scaffolding and (no output) placeholders

question: Should this shared reply sanitizer/normalizer change land after clean or triaged CI, or should maintainers require narrower stripping semantics or live Telegram proof first?
rationale: The code path is shared across reply delivery surfaces and changes whether text is delivered or skipped, so green focused tests alone cannot choose the permanent cross-channel delivery contract.

options.title: Land After Clean Checks
options.body: Rerun or triage the two failing broad compact shards, then merge if maintainers accept the shared sanitizer and `empty-tool-output` contract.

options.title: Request Telegram Proof
options.body: Ask for a short Telegram Desktop proof if maintainers want visual transport confirmation in addition to the current production-function terminal proof.

options.title: Pause For Narrower Semantics
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want a different marker contract or owner boundary for leaked prompt scaffolding before changing shared delivery behavior.

recommendation.title: Land After Clean Checks
recommendation.body: Rerun or triage the two failing broad compact shards, then merge if maintainers accept the shared sanitizer and `empty-tool-output` contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent and historical work on the reply normalizer, dispatcher split, and agent runtime boundary makes this the strongest routing candidate for the shared delivery contract decision.
